title: Anti-higher-order topological insulators
authors: Cheng-Ming Miao, Yu-Hao Wan, Ying-Tao Zhang, Qing-Feng Sun
abstract: Duality is a fundamental concept in physics that connects complementary opposites like particles and holes. Similarly, while topological states in topological insulators localize at boundaries, the existence and nature of their dual counterparts remain unexplored. Here, we introduce anti-topological states as the dual of topological states, exemplified by anti-higher-order topological insulators. Unlike higher-order topological insulators, where states localize at corners, anti-higher-order topological insulators host states along edges but absent at corners, realizing an inverted distribution of states. We demonstrate this phenomenon in a bilayer Chern insulator with opposite Chern numbers, where the band inversion surfaces enclose distinct high-symmetry points. The topological invariant distinguishing these phases is given by the topological charges enclosed by band inversion surfaces. This work establishes anti-topology as a new paradigm, opening a chapter in topological research.
summary: This paper introduces anti-higher-order topological insulators (anti-HOTIs) as the dual counterpart to conventional topological insulators. By analyzing a bilayer Chern insulator model, the authors demonstrate that anti-HOTIs exhibit a unique state distribution where edge states exist but corner states are suppressed. This work establishes anti-topology as a new theoretical framework for topological materials research.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need to explore the dual counterpart of topological states, introducing the concept of anti-topological states and anti-higher-order topological insulators (anti-HOTIs).
main_result: The authors establish anti-topology as a new paradigm, demonstrating that anti-HOTIs host states along most boundaries but are characteristically absent at the corners, unlike conventional HOTIs.
method: The study uses theoretical modeling based on bilayer Chern insulator Hamiltonians and analyzes the topological invariant defined by the charges enclosed by the Band Inversion Surfaces (BIS).
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a bilayer Hamiltonian applied to a Chern insulator, incorporating components derived from a modified Qi–Wu–Zhang (QWZ) model. The analysis is performed on nanoribbons and nanoflakes.
key_observables: The topological invariant is the set of topological charges enclosed by the BIS; key observables include the gap magnitude and the spatial distribution of edge/anti-corner states.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the Chern numbers enclosed by the BIS at high-symmetry points ($\Gamma, X, Y, M$), and the system parameters $B$ and $J$ in the phase diagram analysis.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system preserves inversion symmetry, which helps pin the topological charges at specific high-symmetry points in the Brillouin Zone.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic difference between HOT (corner states) and anti-HOT (anti-corner states), show band structures of nanoribbons at varying angles, and present phase diagrams mapping the anti-HOT phase based on enclosed topological charges.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the concept of anti-topology via duality, develops the model using a bilayer Hamiltonian, calculates the topological invariant using BIS analysis, and finally demonstrates the anti-HOT phase through numerical simulations and phase diagram construction.
why_interesting: The concept of anti-topology provides a new framework for classifying topological phases, which is highly relevant to understanding boundary physics in condensed matter systems, potentially leading to novel material designs.
